S10.01.needs: a Free account or a paid account
S10.01.note: The sidebar control that opens this page was not confirmed; WebAppShell.tsx has a comment about the New project control, not its label.
steps: Sign in and open the Projects page (apps/web/app/chat/projects/page.tsx).
Click "New project".
In the "Create project" dialog, type a name and click "Create project".
Check that the new project appears in the Projects list, compared with Expected.
S10.01.where: Projects page > New project > Create project dialog

steps: Open a conversation.
Click the conversation title in the header to open the menu, then click "Rename".
Or hover a row in the sidebar, open its menu and click "Rename".
Type a new title, press Enter, and check the new title is shown in the header and sidebar.
S10.02.where: Chat title (Conversation options button) > Rename, or sidebar row > Rename

S10.03.needs: at least one project in the account
S10.03.note: The item is shown only when the account has at least one project; once in a project the label reads "Change project".
steps: Open a conversation that is not in a project.
Open the title menu or the row menu and hover "Move to project".
Click a project name in the submenu.
Check the conversation now shows under that project in the sidebar.
S10.03.where: Chat title menu > Move to project, or sidebar row > Move to project

S10.04.note: The menu wording is "Duplicate as branch", a fork of the chat; no project-duplicate control was found in the menu. I did not confirm the success message.
steps: Open a conversation with at least one message.
Open the title menu and click "Duplicate as branch".
Look for the new copy in the sidebar and for any message saying where it is.
Compare with Expected: an independent copy that names its location.
S10.04.where: Chat title menu > Duplicate as branch

S10.05.note: Archive has no confirm dialog; it confirms with the toast. The sidebar archive filter label was not found in the files checked.
steps: Hover a conversation in the sidebar and open its menu.
Click "Archive".
Look for the toast "Chat archived" with "Undo" and "View archived".
Compare with Expected: archiving confirms, offers undo and points to archived items.
Hover a conversation in the sidebar and open its menu.
Click "Delete".
Look for a dialog titled "Delete conversation?" that shows the conversation title in quotes.
Click Cancel first and check nothing is removed; compare with Expected.

S10.07.note: No separate permanent-delete control was found; the one delete dialog carries the irreversible warning. Whether a second confirmation exists is not shown in the code I read.
steps: Open a conversation's row menu and click "Delete".
Read the dialog "Delete conversation?" for the words "This cannot be undone."
Check whether a second confirmation appears before anything is removed.
Compare with Expected.
S10.07.where: Sidebar row > Delete (the dialog says it cannot be undone)

S10.08.note: The header Share button is referred to in a code comment; its visible label was not checked.
steps: Open a conversation with messages.
Click "Share…" in the title menu (or the header Share button).
Read the dialog title "Share conversation" and the audience text, for example "Anyone with the link".
Click "Copy" and check the link is copied and the dialog states who can open it.
S10.08.where: Chat title menu > Share…, or the Share button in the chat header

S10.10.needs: a chat that has produced an artifact
S10.10.note: Takedown control was not confirmed by its visible label in the files read.
steps: Generate an artifact in a chat so the artifact panel opens.
Click the "Publish" action in the artifact panel.
Click the "Share" button in the panel to see the sharing choices.
Check that a link appears with copy, the audience options and a way to take it down; compare with Expected.

labels.text: Published. Copy the link from the bar below.

S10.11.needs: a chat that has produced a generated page or app
S10.11.note: Same control as S10.10; the page does not show a separate publish dialog in the code read.
steps: Generate a web page or app in a chat so it appears as an artifact.
Click "Publish" in the artifact panel.
Wait for the toast "Published. Copy the link from the bar below." or "Published · link copied to clipboard".
Open the link shown in the bar below and compare with Expected: a live URL.

S10.12.needs: a conversation with messages and an existing shared link
S10.12.note: Expiry is set when the link is created; the code did not show a way to change expiry on an existing link.
steps: Share a conversation with Share… and create the link.
Look at the expiry choices "1 day", "7 days" and "30 days" and the audience choice "Anyone with the link".
Change the audience or click "Revoke all links" and confirm.
Check the link shows its access and stops working after revoking; compare with Expected.
S10.12.where: Chat title menu > Share… > Anyone with the link (audience) and expiry choice

S10.13.needs: a workspace owner or admin account
S10.13.note: The visible navigation label for the team section was not found in the settings list (it is keyed as team in apps/web/features/settings/components/WebSettingsModal.tsx); the path is given from the section title.
steps: Open Settings and go to the team section.
Type an email in the "Invitee email" field and choose a role ("Member role", "Viewer role" or "Admin role").
Click the invite button and check "Pending invitations" lists the invite with revoke and renew actions.
Compare with Expected.

S10.14.needs: a workspace owner or admin account and a second member account
steps: Open Settings and the team section as an owner or admin.
On a member row, pick a new role from the role menu ("Viewer role", "Member role" or "Admin role").
In the "Change member role?" dialog, confirm.
Check the member row shows the new role; compare with Expected.
S10.14.where: Settings > Team section > member row role menu

S10.15.needs: the owner account and a second member account
steps: Open Settings and the team section as the owner.
In the card "Transfer ownership", pick another member and the role you keep.
Click "Transfer ownership" and confirm the "Transfer ownership?" dialog.
Check that the other member now shows as owner; compare with Expected.

S10.16.needs: a Free or paid account; a connected app for the app option
S10.16.note: The control that starts a research run was not located, so the entry point is not confirmed.
steps: Start a research run in a chat.
When the research plan appears, read "Sources for this run" or "Searching the whole web. Add a source to narrow it."
Click "Add a source" and pick the sources (connected apps, files, or web) to allow.
Check the plan lists only the chosen sources; compare with Expected.
S10.16.where: Research run plan > Add a source

S10.17.note: The + control's own label was not checked.
steps: In the chat composer, click the + control.
Click "Add photos & files", then "Upload from device".
Pick one or more files in the device file chooser.
Check the picked files appear as attachments on the message before sending.
S10.17.where: Composer > + (Add photos & files) > Upload from device

S10.18.needs: an outside account for the service (for example Google)
S10.18.note: Some services show "Available on desktop and CLI" instead of a connect button.
steps: Open Settings and then Connectors.
Open a service and click "Connect" (or "Add API key" for key-based services).
Complete the service's sign-in or key entry in the window or form that opens.
Check the service now shows as connected; compare with Expected.

S10.19.needs: a connection that has expired (cannot be made on demand)
S10.19.note: The reconnect text reads "needs reconnecting. Its tools stop until you do; its settings are kept." An expired connection is needed, and the tester cannot easily create one.
steps: Open Settings and then Connectors.
Find a service whose text says it needs reconnecting.
Click "Reconnect" and complete the authorization again.
Check the service is connected again and its settings are still there; compare with Expected.
S10.19.where: Settings > Connectors > (service that needs reconnecting) > Reconnect

S10.20.needs: a service with more than one connected account
S10.20.note: Only the API route apps/web/app/api/connectors/[connectorId]/accounts/route.ts was found. I searched apps/web/features and packages/ui/ui/src for "Make default", "Default account" and "Use this account" and found no matching visible control.

steps: Open Settings and then Plugins.
Open a plugin and read its details.
Click "Install".
Check the plugin shows as installed ("Installed") in the account or workspace; compare with Expected.

S10.22.needs: a plugin that asks for permissions
S10.22.note: The code shows a permissions section on the plugin detail page; a separate accept dialog was not found in the files read.
steps: Open Settings, then Plugins, and open a plugin.
Scroll to the "Permissions" section and read the list of permissions.
Compare with Expected: the list must be shown before the install or update is accepted.
Note whether an accept step follows the list, since the code read shows only the list.

S10.23.needs: an installed plugin that has a newer version
S10.23.note: The button label that applies the update was not found in the files read; only the badge and version text were found.
steps: Open Settings, then Plugins.
Look for a plugin marked "Update available".
Open it and read the "Update to" version text and what changed.
Apply the update and compare with Expected.
S10.23.where: Settings > Plugins > (plugin with an update) > Update

S10.24.note: The button that opens the New skill dialog was not found in the files read.
steps: Open Settings, then Skills.
Click the control that creates a new skill, which opens the "New skill" dialog.
Click "Import a SKILL.md" and pick a SKILL.md file (.md or text).
Check the name, description and instructions fields fill from the file; then click "Create skill" and compare with Expected.
S10.24.where: Settings > Skills > New skill > Import a SKILL.md

S10.25.note: The edit dialog exists in apps/web/features/skills/components/SkillEditorDialog.tsx (title "Edit skill", save button "Save changes"), but the control that opens it for an existing skill was not found in the files read.

S10.26.needs: a chat with an image or tool use, and two or more models
S10.26.note: The warning title is built from a template string ("Switch to" plus the model name), and the model picker's own label was not checked.
steps: Attach an image, or start a chat with tools or a long conversation.
Open the model picker in the composer and pick a model that cannot handle it.
Read the warning "Switch to <model name>?" with its reasons.
Click "Keep <current model>" to cancel or "Switch anyway" to switch; compare with Expected.
S10.26.where: Composer > model picker > choose a model that cannot take this chat

labels.text: Older messages will be left out of the next reply.

S10.27.needs: a conversation large enough to pass the model's context budget (no test account setting found)
S10.27.note: The warning text only says older messages will be left out; the code shows no trim, compact or new-chat action, so the 'what to do' part of Expected is missing.
steps: Sign in and open a conversation with many long messages, or paste a long text into the message box until the conversation is large
Look at the strip above the message box, under the model name
Read the warning text and compare it with Expected: a clear warning with what to do (trim, compact, new chat)
S10.27.where: Open a long conversation > the warning appears in the composer footer above the message box (no button)

labels.text: Usage budget exhausted for this billing period. Upgrade your plan or add credits.

S10.28.needs: an account whose usage budget is exhausted
S10.28.note: The code text names no reset time; a reset time and a named limit were not found in this text, only in the paywall card code (apps/web/features/chat/components/InlinePaywallCard.tsx), which I did not confirm is the card shown here.
steps: Sign in on a Free or paid account whose usage budget is used up for this period
Open a chat and send a message
Read the notice that appears in the chat and check it shows which limit was reached, when it resets, and what to do (Upgrade or add credits)
S10.28.where: Send a message in chat once the plan's usage budget is used up; the message shows a limit notice

S10.29.needs: a paid or Free account; checkout also needs an access code while the billing waitlist is on
S10.29.note: Owner-held: the code says paid checkout needs a redeemed access code while AGI_BILLING_WAITLIST_OPEN is unset, so payment may not complete for a tester; the purchase is a hosted checkout page, not an in-app dialog.
steps: Open Settings from the account menu, then choose Billing
Find the section titled Buy credits
Choose a pack or type an amount and press the checkout button
Compare with Expected: a purchase dialog lets the user buy credits and complete payment

S10.30.note: The upgrade comparison dialog exists with the title 'Upgrade your plan' (or 'Upgrade to <plan>'), but I did not trace which button opens it, so the path is unknown.

S10.31.needs: a paid account billed through Stripe that is not already ending
S10.31.note: The button opens the Stripe billing portal (openPortal('cancel')), so the confirmation and end date are shown by that outside page, not by the app.
steps: Open Settings from the account menu, then choose Billing
Find the Cancel plan button in the plan area (shown only on a paid plan billed through Stripe and not already ending)
Press Cancel plan and compare with Expected: a dialog says when access ends and asks to confirm

S10.32.needs: a paid account with Stripe billing for the portal to open
S10.32.note: The button opens the Stripe billing portal, so card entry happens on that outside page, not in an app dialog.
steps: Open Settings from the account menu, then choose Billing
Find the payment method area and press the button; its label is Add payment method when no card is saved, Manage cards when one is, and Open billing portal when the list fails to load
Compare with Expected: a dialog lets the user add or replace the card on file
S10.32.where: Settings > Billing > Add payment method (or Manage cards / Open billing portal)

S10.33.needs: an account with a passkey or an email code for its second check
S10.33.note: The 'Confirm it is you' step-up dialog exists and offers email code, passkey or password, but I did not trace which sensitive action opens it (useStepUp hook at apps/web/features/settings/hooks/useStepUp.tsx), so the tester's path is unknown.

S10.34.note: Searched apps/web, apps/desktop and packages/ui for microphone wording: found only error text after access fails (apps/desktop/src/hooks/useVoiceTranscription.ts) and an OS permission request (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/systemPermissions.ts); no explanation shown before first use was found.

S10.35.needs: the desktop app and a screen with more than one window open
S10.35.note: The composer button label was not confirmed (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:1832 was not read in full).
steps: Sign in to the desktop app and open a chat
Press the screen-share control in the message box (its exact label was not traced)
Read the native dialog: it lists each screen and window, plus Cancel
Pick one and compare with Expected: the chosen screen or window is the only one captured
S10.35.where: Chat > screen share control in the composer > native dialog 'Share a screen or window'

S10.36.needs: the desktop app and a task that triggers computer control
S10.36.note: Button label for 'Allow ... this session' is built from the allow label, which I did not read; the code marks high-impact permissions as lasting only until quit.
steps: Open the desktop app and ask the assistant to do a task that uses the computer or browser
When the native dialog 'Permission required' appears, read the text 'Allow ... to ...?' and the high-impact note if shown
Choose Deny, Allow this session, or Always allow (Never allow appears only for high-impact permissions)
Compare with Expected: the dialog says what it can do and only a granted choice lets it continue
S10.36.where: Not a menu: appears the first time the assistant tries to control the computer or browser; native dialog 'Permission required'

S10.37.needs: the desktop app and a local folder to pick
S10.37.note: The dialog text says 'Desktop asks your permission before it reads anything inside'; the separate permission prompt (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/dispatcher.ts:2312) was not traced to its visible words.
steps: In the desktop app, open a chat and press the + button in the message box
Choose Attach from local folder
Read the dialog text and press Choose a folder to approve a folder
Pick a file inside and compare with Expected: the app asked permission before reading the folder
S10.37.where: Message box + button > Attach from local folder > Choose a folder

labels.text: Running on this device. Approve it if your desktop asks.

S10.38.needs: a task that needs a tool approval
S10.38.note: The card also has an 'Approve for chat' option for lower-risk actions (not 'Always allow' text); I did not confirm the exact visible label for it.
steps: Ask the assistant to do a task that calls a tool which needs approval
When the tool card appears in the chat, read the action it shows
Press Approve or Deny on that one card
Compare with Expected: only that single call is approved or denied
S10.38.where: Chat > a tool action card shows Approve and Deny buttons while it waits

labels.text: Private data from this chat could be sent outside AGI. Check where it goes before you allow it.

S10.39.needs: a task that sends chat data outside, such as a connector or web action
S10.39.note: The warning text names no destination; the code that decides when it appears (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-loop.ts:1086) was not read in full, so which tasks trigger it is unconfirmed.
steps: Ask the assistant to do a task that could send private chat data to an outside service
When the approval card appears, read the warning text
Check that it says where the data goes before you press Approve
Compare with Expected: the user is asked to approve the transfer and told what goes where
S10.39.where: Chat > tool approval card, the high-risk warning text

S10.40.needs: a paid plan (the code shows 'Remote Control comes with paid plans' otherwise) and the mobile app on a phone
S10.40.note: Owner notes say Remote Control is hidden in the first mobile release; I did not check that in code, so visibility is unconfirmed.
steps: In the desktop app, open Settings from the account menu, then choose Capabilities
Find Remote Control and press Pair a phone
Read the pairing dialog 'Pair your phone' and the code or QR shown
Compare with Expected: the code is for one phone only and is tied to the signed-in account
S10.40.where: Settings > Capabilities > Remote Control > Pair a phone

S10.41.note: The exact open path for project settings was not traced; the warning itself is in packages/ui/ui/src/primitives/UnsavedChanges.tsx.
steps: Open an editor such as a project's settings
Change a field without saving
Close the editor or leave the page
Compare with Expected: the dialog 'Discard unsaved changes?' offers Keep editing and Discard
S10.41.where: Any editor with unsaved edits (for example project settings), then close it

S10.42.needs: a second tab or device signed in to the same account
S10.42.note: Merging is not offered; the dialog offers only keeping one version.
steps: Open the same chat in two tabs or on two devices, both signed in to one account
Type in the message box in tab 1 but do not send
Type a different draft in the same chat in tab 2 and wait
Return to tab 1 and compare with Expected: the dialog 'Choose which draft to keep' shows both drafts and offers Keep this version or Use the other version
S10.42.where: Two browser tabs or devices on the same chat: edit the unsent draft in one, then in the other, when the conflict appears

S10.43.note: The export format options in the dialog (EnhancedExportDialog) were not read, and the title menu's on-screen position was not traced.
steps: Open a chat and open its title menu (the conversation title at the top)
Choose Export…
Read the export dialog and pick a format
Compare with Expected: a file is exported for the chosen format

labels.text: Reported. Thank you: our trust and safety team will review it.

S10.44.needs: a chat with an assistant answer
S10.44.note: No reason is asked for: the code files the report at once as 'harmful' by default (no reason dialog), which differs from Expected.
steps: Open a chat with an answer from the assistant
Open that answer's menu and choose Report this response
Read the toast that appears
Compare with Expected: the report is sent to the moderation team after the user gives a reason
S10.44.where: Chat > an assistant answer > its menu > Report this response

S10.45.note: The account menu's opening control was not traced; the feedback dialog itself is also opened from a Feedback button in the composer.
steps: Open the account menu from your name or avatar
Choose Get help, then Send feedback
Pick a Feedback type, type a message, and press send
Compare with Expected: the message is saved to the team's feedback store and the dialog confirms it
S10.45.where: Account menu > Get help > Send feedback

labels.text: Send error reports, with sensitive fields removed.

S10.46.note: It is a switch, not a dialog; the description does not list what is included, which Expected asks for.
steps: Open Settings from the account menu, then choose Privacy
Find the switch Share crash and error reports and read its description
Turn it on or off, then check the saved state stays after reload
Compare with Expected: the user is told what is included before choosing
S10.46.where: Settings > Privacy > Share crash and error reports

S10.47.needs: an account that can request an export (email delivery is mentioned in the code)
S10.47.note: It is a row in the Privacy page, not a dialog; the code says the link works for a fixed number of hours and may be emailed.
steps: Open Settings from the account menu, then choose Privacy
Find the Export data row and press the Export data button
Wait while it shows Preparing…, then look for Download your export or Download part N of M
Compare with Expected: the download link is delivered and opens as a file

S10.48.needs: an account that is not blocked by a plan or a pending payment
S10.48.note: Deletion is scheduled, not immediate, and the dialog can be cancelled through Cancel deletion before the deadline; the full list of what is deleted was not read from the dialog.
steps: Open Settings from the account menu, then choose Account
Press Delete account (the button is disabled when a plan or payment blocks it)
In the dialog Delete your account?, read the text and type DELETE in the box
Press the confirm button and compare with Expected: the dialog says what is deleted and deletion is scheduled, with a way to cancel before the deadline
